decisions.name: the code that runs is admitted
a refusal blocks the digest even when it is authored here
a refusal blocks the digest even with a store snapshot and a healthy canary
a refusal of another digest does not matter
the earliest refusal is named, a tie goes to the lower id
a store snapshot admits at once
a snapshot of another digest does not
a canary healthy for the set time admits the follower
a canary one second short of the set time keeps the follower waiting
a canary seen for the first time makes the follower wait the whole time
a half second short rounds up to a whole second
the healthiest of several canaries decides
a canary with a stale attestation is no canary
a canary with a fresh attestation 60 s old still counts
a canary that runs a fallback code is no canary
a canary with sync off is no canary
a canary of another group is no canary
a retired canary is no canary
the own attestation is never a canary
code written entirely here goes first at once
a canary running the code outranks authorship
the deadlock: the closure was written on three origins, the group server waits the set time first
the group server one second before its time
the group server at its time goes first
a worker waits behind the group server and the lower ids
a worker at half its turn
the third candidate goes after two turns
the second candidate waits one turn
a stale server does not lead, the lowest fresh id does
with a stale server the next id waits one turn behind the lowest
without a server the lowest id leads
two candidates racing at the same moment: the lower id goes
two candidates racing at the same moment: the higher id waits
an origin with sync off never leads
an origin on a fallback code never leads
a retired origin never leads
an origin of another group never leads
a writer clock 30 s ahead still counts as fresh
a writer clock 61 s ahead is stale
ordering is bytewise: m10 comes after m02
a lone origin goes after the wait
a lone origin before the wait

trackers.name: the time starts at the first reading and grows with the readings
a gap longer than the freshness window starts the time again
a gap of exactly the freshness window keeps the time
an unhealthy reading forgets the origin and a healthy one starts again
a stale attestation is not healthy
other codes, sync off, the own attestation and a missing origin are not healthy
two origins have their own times
